description:
You are a labor economist preparing a wage determination model using Current Population Survey (CPS) data. Before submitting your analysis for peer review, you need to check for multicollinearity among the regressors.

Gretl is open with the CPS wage dataset loaded from /home/ga/Documents/gretl_data/cps_wages.gdt. The dataset contains 60 observations with these variables:
- wage: hourly wage rate in dollars
- educ: years of education
- exper: years of work experience
- female: 1 if female, 0 if male
- black: 1 if black, 0 otherwise
- metro: 1 if metropolitan area
- south: 1 if southern US region
- west: 1 if western US region

Write and execute a Gretl script that:
1. Opens the dataset /home/ga/Documents/gretl_data/cps_wages.gdt
2. Generates a new variable lwage = ln(wage) (natural log of wage)
3. Generates a new variable exper2 = exper * exper (experience squared)
4. Runs OLS regression: lwage on const, educ, exper, exper2, female, black, metro, south, west
5. Computes Variance Inflation Factors (VIF) using the vif command
6. Saves the regression output to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/wage_model.txt
7. Saves the VIF results to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/vif_results.txt

Save the script itself as /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/vif_analysis.inp

All three files must exist after execution:
- /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/vif_analysis.inp (the script)
- /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/wage_model.txt (regression results)
- /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/vif_results.txt (VIF values for all 8 regressors)
